title: rapid-sdk-playground-runbook-sketch
content:
Purpose:
A compact runbook for running a short (30-90m) interactive SDK playground session for engineers and PMs. Goal is low-friction: get people to call the Redwood API locally, see streaming, try embeddings, and exercise the telemetry hooks that tie back to Console. Focus is empathy-first: minimal setup, clear recovery steps, and a few guided experiments that teach performance/cost tradeoffs.

Audience:
- New hires (engineer/ML engineer) doing first-week ramp
- Developer advocates running workshops
- Solutions engineers doing quick customer demos

Key constraints / design goals:
- 10 minute full-setup from a clean laptop (mac/linux) ideally using only Docker + a single env var (REDWOOD_API_KEY).
- Provide both CLI-first and code-first paths (js + py example snippets).
- Include a lightweight failure-mode checklist (token errors, rate limits, kwarg mismatch for streaming).
- Keep the runbook single-file for workshop leaders; external deeper docs linked.

Quick path (recommended order)
1) Pre-reqs: install Docker OR node >=18 or python3.10, git.
2) Clone starter repo: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-playground
3) Set API key: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=redwood_demo_xxx (or use .env)
4) Start local proxy (optional): docker compose up -d proxy (proxy rewrites host for private envs)
5) Run quick CLI demo (30s): node ./examples/cli/generate.js --model small --prompt "Summarize: Redwood inference is..."
6) Try streaming: node ./examples/streaming/stream-demo.js --model chatstream
7) Try embeddings: python3 examples/embeddings/emb-index.py data/sample-notes.md
8) View telemetry: open Console > Playgrounds > recent-session (or link to session id printed by CLI)

Hands-on experiments (30–45m total)
- Latency vs batch size (10–15m): use batch tester script to send 1->32 concurrent small requests and plot p50/p95. Note when batching reduces cost but increases tail latency.
- Cache demo (5m): repeat a prompt and show prefix/KV cache hit counter in Console (explain TTL).
- Quantized model swap (10m): switch from float32 model to int8 variant, compare cost and small hallucination differences (use curated prompts).
- Structured output + tool-calling (10m): demonstrate function call pattern and the SDK helper that validates JSON schema return.

Commands & snippets (copy/paste friendly)
- Clone + setup:
  git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-playground && cd sdk-playground
  cp .env.example .env && # edit REDWOOD_API_KEY
  npm ci || pip install -r requirements.txt

- Node quick generate:
  node examples/cli/generate.js --model redwood-small --prompt "Write a 2-sentence product blurb for Redwood Inference."

- Python streaming example:
  python3 examples/streaming/stream_client.py --model chatstream --prompt-file examples/prompts/onboarding.txt

- Basic embedding flow (python):
  python3 examples/embeddings/emb_index.py --upsert data/notes.json --query "how does caching work?"

Telemetry & observability (what to show in 5m)
- Where to look: Console > Sessions (filter by playground-tag) -> click session id -> token-level cost and p50/p95 charts.
- Quick hooks: pass X-Client-Session header in SDK to link session to Console. CLI sets this automatically when --session-id is provided.
- Common metrics to surface: requests/sec, tokens-in, tokens-out, p50/p95 latency, cache-hit-rate, quantized-fallbacks.

Failure modes & recovery (quick checklist)
- 401 / invalid key: check .env, ensure team API key not org-scoped; run: REDWOOD_API_KEY=redwood_demo_xxx node examples/cli/check_key.js
- Rate-limited: observe 429 -> wait/backoff, show how to throttle via --rate-limit flag or set route-level quota in Console.
- Streaming stalls: smaller batch/window, check network, restart local proxy (docker compose restart proxy).
- Schema validation errors on tool calls: show sample schema mismatch quick-fix (update schemas/ functions.json).

Leader tips (notes to self)
- Start session by describing the product thesis in one sentence: serving > model.
- Keep one laptop as "fallback" with pre-run docker compose for demos that may fail on attendees' machines.
- Encourage attendees to open Console while running to see live telemetry — that visual link is a big "aha".
- Timebox experiments strictly. Have a 5min buffer for common install issues.

Suggested workshop schedule (40m):
- 0–5m: intro + goals
- 5–12m: quick CLI generate + streaming demo
- 12–25m: choose one deep path (embeddings or quantization) + guided exercises
- 25–35m: telemetry walkthrough + dashboard tips
- 35–40m: Q&A + next steps (invite to SDK discord channel)

Open questions / TODOs
- Should the repo include prebuilt Docker images for mac M1 edge cases? (Q: infra?)
- Add a single-file docker entrypoint that does key injection and opens a static HTML telemetry view?
- Decide canonical session-id header name and ensure SDKs all set it consistently (follow-up ticket SDKPLAY-20).
- Workshop scoring rubric: how to measure success? (suggest: attendees who finish embedding lab + can find session in Console).

Links / references
- Starter repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-playground
- Workshop slides (WIP): https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1playgrounDdemo
- Telemetry design notes: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/DEX/Playground+Design+Notes

Appendix (quick cheats)
- If an attendee is on corporate network blocking Docker: recommend node path & portable proxy script.
- If session hits quota: demo switching to a dedicated-plan model alias to show no-rate-limit behavior (demo only).

Notes-to-self (raw)
- Make examples less chatty; add one-liners for every script so README is scannable.
- Add a "reset environment" script that clears local cache and logs to reproduce cache-hit demo reliably.
- Flesh out embed example with a tiny semantic search UI (single html file) so product folks can see UX implications.

-- end runbook sketch --
summary: Runbook sketch for a fast interactive SDK playground used in onboarding and workshops; includes setup, hands-on experiments, telemetry pointers, failure checklist, schedule, and open questions.
